payload.title: Drain owned command collector tasks after stream failure
payload.summary: P2 execution-resource cleanup. A deterministic create_subprocess_exec fake gives stdout a RuntimeError and keeps stderr.read blocked. Public CommandExecutor.start/await returns the original failure, closes events and reports a complete handle after killing/reaping the fake immediate child, yet one owned _read_stream task remains pending and uncancelled. Existing test_handle stream-failure fixture gives stderr immediate EOF, hiding this state. asyncio.gather propagates one child exception without cancelling surviving collectors.
payload.benefit: Within existing Commands ownership, cancel and await every owned stream/input collector before returning terminal failure, cancellation or timeout; preserve the original exception and child cleanup semantics. Add deterministic blocked-sibling and blocked-input fault schedules plus real normal/timeout/cancellation controls, single execution/repeated awaits and closed event behavior. No orphan collector may remain after failed execute returns. Do not add retries, process-tree authority, a general executor or a new lifecycle framework.
payload.uncertainty: This task-lifetime defect is established with explicit I/O fault fakes, not an observed leaked real child or historical corrupted run. Real managed timeout and cancellation controls passed; side effects remain after cancellation. Commands has actual CommandTool/Qwen/Git/check callers; live events have no maintained application consumer found by the bounded caller search. B-0041 remains the broader execution-local lifecycle investigation.
dependencies: Existing owner/API contracts; separately authorized bounded production repair; independent permanent regressions and full unchanged protected validation.
